DESIGN §3.1 defines the Anchor primitive. `class Anchor` is the canonical Pydantic model — its docstring cites §3.1 explicitly.
DESIGN §3.1 enumerates the three anchor types (section, code_in_doc, code). `AnchorType` is the StrEnum encoding that taxonomy.

DESIGN §3.2 Layer 2 fingerprint section anchors carry `(normalized_heading_path, content_hash)`. `fingerprint_simhash` produces the 64-bit SimHash used as the AST/structural fingerprint stored on every anchor (Anchor.fingerprint_simhash field).

DESIGN §3.3 fuzzy match algorithm thresholds: embedding cosine ≥ 0.85, SimHash Jaccard ≥ 0.7. FuzzyMatchConfig encodes exactly these defaults (embedding_threshold=0.85, simhash_jaccard_threshold=0.7, plus migration variant).

DESIGN §3.3 "prior-hash override": prior_from/to_content_hash on a link records what each endpoint hashed to before rebase. `_resolve_changed`'s docstring cites §3.3 and implements the override (uses prior_*_content_hash for comparison so rename-with-edit shows as drift, not fresh).
DESIGN §3.3 "Same-file constraint by default. Cross-file rebase opt-in via index.cross_file_rebase: true". IndexConfig.cross_file_rebase is the exact config field implementing this opt-in.

DESIGN §3.4 two-tier embedding splits parent anchors into sub-chunks. `SubChunk` is the Pydantic model encoding this — docstring cites §3.4 explicitly, and the comment notes sub-chunks are not separate drift units.

DESIGN §3.4 splits parent anchors into sub-chunks for embedding. `chunk_anchor` is the function that performs this split — docstring cites §3.4 and handles both SECTION (split into multiple) and CODE/CODE_IN_DOC (single chunk) per the spec.

DESIGN §3.5.1 defines the event record schema (op, link_id, event_id, ts, from/to/type/hashes, supersedes, reason). LinkRecord is the Pydantic model encoding this schema — docstring cites §3.5.1 explicitly.
DESIGN §3.5.1 defines op as one of "upsert" or "delete". LinkOp is the StrEnum encoding those two values.

DESIGN §3.5.2 defines replay rules 1, 2, 6 (file order = last-wins; baseline first then overlay; merge-conflict detection on broken supersedes chains). LinkStore.replay implements all three rules with explicit citations in the docstring.
DESIGN §3.5.2 produces an "active link table" + "merge-conflicts" output. ReplayResult is the dataclass encoding both — docstring cites §3.5.2 rule 6 for merge_conflicts.

DESIGN §3.5.4 defines the two-phase atomic promotion protocol: append to baseline + write marker, atomic overlay rewrite, delete marker. `promote_overlay_to_baseline` implements exactly this protocol — docstring cites §3.5.4 v3.1 explicitly with all 3 phases.

DESIGN §3.5.0 defines overlay slug derivation: branch name URL-encoded with quote(safe=''), detached-HEAD fallback, sha256 truncation for long branches. `derive_overlay_slug` implements this exact algorithm — docstring cites §3.5.0 explicitly.
DESIGN §3.6 defines the canonical link-type vocabulary: implements, tests, examples, mirrors, derives-from, references. LinkType is the StrEnum with exactly these 6 values.

DESIGN §4.1 v3.1 specifies the hybrid retrieval algorithm: vector ANN + BM25 with parent promotion + RRF fusion. `hybrid_search` is the canonical implementation — its docstring cites §4.1 v3.1 and walks through each step.

DESIGN §4.2 defines the Anchor packet returned by search. `AnchorPacket` is the Pydantic envelope — docstring cites §4.2 explicitly with all required fields (anchor, score, evidence_excerpt, links, content_truncated).

DESIGN §4.2 turns search results into AnchorPackets (load parent anchor, compute evidence excerpt, truncate content, etc.). `build_anchor_packet` implements all 6 steps from §4.2 — docstring cites §4.2 with numbered steps matching the spec.

DESIGN §5.1 defines the drift status taxonomy (fresh, spec-changed, code-changed, both-changed, broken-source/target, merge-conflict, drift-unknown). `evaluate_link_drift` is the function computing drift status per the §5.1 precedence ladder — docstring cites §5.1 post-v3.1 with all 9 steps.
DESIGN §5.1 v3.1 introduces the DriftStatus enum. `DriftStatus` is the StrEnum encoding all 8 statuses with the exact spec-defined string values.
DESIGN §5.2 v3.1 defines drift_score and coverage_score formulas. `compute_drift_summary` implements exactly those formulas — docstring cites §5.2 v3.1 with the weighted-sum calculation.

DESIGN §5.2 emits raw counts per drift status alongside the scores. `DriftCounts` is the Pydantic model encoding those counts (broken_source, broken_target, merge_conflict, both_changed, spec_changed, code_changed, drift_unknown, semantic_drift_flagged, fresh, total).

DESIGN §5.3 defines transitive code drift via LSP callHierarchy/outgoingCalls. `compute_closure` is the canonical implementation — uses prepareCallHierarchy + outgoingCalls with BFS bounded by transitive_max_depth, returns ClosureResult with status enum from §5.3 status table.
DESIGN §5.3 specifies the closure-hash status enum (complete, partial, unsupported, lsp_unavailable, lsp_error). `TransitiveHashStatus` is the StrEnum encoding these 5 values.

DESIGN §5.4 defines content_hash canonicalization: BOM strip, CRLF→LF, trailing whitespace stripping, single trailing newline. `canonicalize_content` is the canonical implementation referenced from Anchor docstring + content_hash().
DESIGN §5.4 produces "sha256:<64 hex>" over canonicalized content. `content_hash` is the helper that does exactly this — docstring cites §5.4 and ContentHash type constraint.

DESIGN §5.5 defines LLM-assisted reconciliation for drifted links. `propose_patch` is the core function — docstring cites §5.5 step 1 for git-diff fetch, calls LLM with system prompt, parses target/diff/explanation per the spec.
DESIGN §5.5 surfaces reconciliation via CLI. The `scry reconcile` command is the user-facing entry — docstring cites §5.5 directly.
DESIGN §6 specifies .scry/config.yaml schema with include/exclude/classify/sections/code_anchors/embeddings/etc. Config is the Pydantic model encoding the full schema with cross-field validation.
DESIGN §6 says a repo participates by adding .scry/config.yaml. `load_config` reads + validates the yaml file — docstring cites §6 directly.
DESIGN §6.1 defines per-file frontmatter overrides (markdown YAML block with scry: key). `parse_frontmatter` is the parser; `Frontmatter` is the validated schema model.

DESIGN §7.1 specifies the index_metadata row in vectors.db. `IndexMetadata` is the Pydantic model encoding all fields (indexed_git_head, indexed_branch, config_hash, embedding_provider/model/dimensions, manifest, etc.) — docstring cites §7.1 directly.

DESIGN §7.2 v3.1 defines auto-reconcile via polling (check git HEAD/dirty files, trigger background re-index). `IndexStateTracker` implements the state machine with transitions to FRESH/STALE_RECONCILING/STALE_WARNED/STALE_NO_WRITE_LOCK per §7.2 transition rules.

DESIGN §7.2 enumerates the index_state values returned in MCP responses. `IndexState` is the StrEnum with all values from the post-v3.1 spec (fresh, stale-reconciling, stale-warned, stale-no-write-lock).

DESIGN §7.2.1 specifies --reembed: surgical embedding-model migration that preserves anchors/links/fingerprints. `Indexer.reembed` implements exactly the 4-step algorithm (prune missing → reconcile vec dims → re-embed batches → atomic metadata swap). Docstring cites §7.2.1 directly.

DESIGN §7.3 invariant 2 requires per-parent atomic transactions for anchor + chunks reindex. `reindex_anchor_with_chunks` performs upsert_anchor + replace_chunks inside a single SQLite transaction — docstring cites §7.3 invariant 2 directly.

DESIGN §7.3 invariant 1 + 3 + 4 require atomic per-parent chunk replacement (delete old + insert new in single txn) so readers never see a mix. `replace_chunks` implements this — docstring cites §7.3 invariants 1, 3, 4.

DESIGN §8 defines the MCP tool surface — 15 tools registered with FastMCP. `MCPServer` is the canonical FastMCP-based server class implementing the full tool surface with leader/follower coordination.

DESIGN §10.2 v3.1 specifies leader election via OS-level advisory lock (fcntl.flock on POSIX, msvcrt.locking on Windows) on .scry/leader.lock with metadata-write ordering. `LeaderLock` class implements exactly this acquisition order — docstring cites §10.2 v3.1 with all 4 steps.
DESIGN §10.3 specifies IPC over Unix socket (POSIX) or named pipe (Windows). `IPCServer` is the leader-side listener; `IPCClient` is the follower-side connector. They form the §10.3 IPC dispatch.

DESIGN §10.3 IPC protocol: follower-side connector forwarding write ops to the leader with idempotency tokens. `IPCClient` implements the request/response framing with serialised call() — the follower-side counterpart of IPCServer.

DESIGN §10.4 cold-start sequence (load config, acquire leader lock, bind IPC, write metadata, recover crash). `MCPServer.start` implements the full cold-start with leader and follower paths — server.py module docstring cites §10.4 v3.1.

DESIGN §15.1 specifies heading extraction rules (ATX/setext, max_heading_depth, fenced-block-aware, empty heading slug fallback). `extract_markdown_with_diagnostics` implements §15.1 — docstring explicitly cites §15.1, §15.2, §15.4.

DESIGN §15.2 specifies code block extraction (lang-tagged with named declarations → code_in_doc anchor). `extract_markdown_with_diagnostics` produces both SECTION and CODE_IN_DOC anchors per §15.1+§15.2.

DESIGN §15.3 ID derivation: slugify rules, fallback for empty/non-ASCII headings, HTML scry-id comment override, sibling collision suffixes. `slugify` is the slug derivation function per §15.3 rules (NFKD → ASCII → lowercase → non-alnum→dash → fallback hash).
DESIGN §15.3 sibling-heading slug collision resolution: first gets bare slug, subsequent get -N suffix. `disambiguate_siblings` is the helper applying §15.3 positional-suffix collision resolution.
